hypothesis: The two prior failures were caused by gait_phase_regularity_reward_weight = -2.5, which overrode stabilising reflexes without improving CV metrics. Resetting regularity to baseline (-1.0) restores stability, while increasing air_time_reward_weight from 0.2 to 0.5 provides a gentler, mechanistically different handle on gait CV: instead of penalising irregular timing after the fact, it directly rewards feet spending time airborne in the healthy 0.05–0.5s window, encouraging a consistent periodic stepping cadence. Keeping shoulder_pitch std at 0.35 (validated safe in both prior runs) costs nothing. Together these should reduce gait_air_cv_mean and gait_contact_cv_mean toward the healthy range without destabilising the robot.
expected_effects: fell_over_rate drops toward 0 past iteration 500 — stability gate passes (reverting the confirmed destabiliser)
gait_air_cv_mean decreases from 0.247 baseline — direct effect of air_time reward encouraging consistent foot lifting cadence
gait_contact_cv_mean decreases from 0.334 baseline — consistent swing timing feeds into more regular contact timing
air_time reward term value increases in late-window metrics — confirms the weight increase is taking effect and the policy is producing more swings in the 0.05–0.5s range

track_linear_velocity reward dips slightly vs baseline — Rule 6 side-effect check: policy allocating some capacity to step cadence vs pure speed matching; if it doesn't dip at all, the air_time change is not doing real work
